report.upstream-programs-maintain-state-: Upstream programs maintain state. Feature encoding connects reference video to real-time neural rendering using bounded caches and chunked autoregression.

report.evidence-4-4-2-5-1-5-3-7-342: Evidence: §4.4.2, §5.1/5.3, §7; demonstrates a running pipeline, without dedicated off-screen evolution or clock-decoupling tests.
report.long-duration-evaluation-in-5-1-5: Long-duration evaluation in §5.1–5.3 targets 30 s and measures reference control, first-frame retention and temporal consistency. It is not an unbounded-map or return-pose evaluation.
report.4-4-2-states-that-the-fixed-simul: §4.4.2 states that the fixed simulation step is independent of generation, but each chunk's progression is stretched so state does not get ahead of generated video. Simulation logic is independent; runtime pacing remains synchronized with video.
report.7-explicitly-identifies-the-lack-: §7 explicitly identifies the lack of dedicated appearance memory and leaves retrieval after long occlusion or revisitation to future work. This is a related-work citation; the project does not depend on it.
report.a-coding-agent-manages-executable: A Coding Agent manages executable world mechanisms with frequent code updates. A lightweight proxy and structured text condition video generation.
report.overlapping-window-continuation-n: · Overlapping-window continuation; no unbounded map algorithm
report.explicit-state-supports-leaving-a: · Explicit state supports leaving and returning; no dedicated evaluation
report.persistent-consequences-are-empha: · Persistent consequences are emphasized; no revisit consistency metrics
report.code-updates-are-decoupled-from-a: · Code updates are decoupled from Agent inference and video frame rates
report.evidence-3-1-4-1-4-2-validates-pr: Evidence: §3.1, §4.1–4.2; validates proxy conditioning and controllable generation; the website shows long videos.
report.3-1-explicitly-discusses-off-scre: §3.1 explicitly discusses off-screen consequences and frequent state updates, separating code execution from Agent inference and video frame rates. Updates may be event-driven or faster than visual generation.
report.4-mainly-validates-proxy-spatiote: §4 mainly validates proxy spatiotemporal control, generalization and visual generation; long video uses overlapping windows. No dedicated independent-clock or long-term off-screen-return experiment was found.
report.code-maintained-persistent-worlds: Code-maintained persistent worlds are an explicit part of the approach. Complex city consequences or unbounded space in examples should not be treated as empirically established capabilities.
report.multiple-agents-construct-an-exec: Multiple Agents construct an executable white-box world. Generated RGB is registered onto existing surfaces by depth backprojection for later views.
report.open-interaction-and-autonomous-e: · Open interaction and autonomous evolution; no unbounded terrain expansion shown
report.360-loop-closure-returns-to-an-of: · 360° loop closure; returns to an off-screen cup
report.wall-marks-and-structure-persist-: · Wall marks and structure persist; no separate revisit metric
report.water-rises-while-out-of-view-no-: · Water rises while out of view; no explicit clock protocol
report.evidence-3-2-4-3-figures-3-5-tabl: Evidence: §3.2, §4.3, Figures 3/5; Table 1 evaluates general consistency, not an independent clock quantitatively.
report.figure-3-returns-to-a-wall-after-: Figure 3 returns to a wall after a 360° rotation and checks marks, structure and appearance. This is explicit qualitative loop-closure validation.
report.figure-5-compares-off-screen-pour: Figure 5 compares off-screen pouring: the water level has risen when the view returns. This directly demonstrates state evolution outside observation.
report.the-paper-emphasizes-evolution-in: The paper emphasizes evolution independent of visual observation, but does not specify or test a fixed-step clock protocol under pause, time scaling or changing render rates. Open interaction does not imply unbounded space.
report.per-frame-geometric-caches-retrie: Per-frame geometric caches retrieve history; geometric correspondence guides attention, and self-enhanced training reduces drift. The output is reconstructed as 3DGS / mesh.
report.arbitrary-length-trajectories-and: · Arbitrary-length trajectories and progressive expansion; all tested routes are finite
report.look-back-examples-and-overall-lo: · Look-back examples and overall long-route metrics, not revisit-only results

report.evidence-4-1-4-2-5-2-5-5-369: Evidence: §4.1–4.2, §5.2/5.5, §6; Figure 3 looks back after approximately 800 frames; Table 1 measures overall quality.
report.4-1-states-that-memory-grows-with: §4.1 states that memory grows with the trajectory, supporting arbitrary-length trajectories and revisitation. This is neither a fixed-map-size guarantee nor an unlimited-scale experiment.
report.figure-3-in-5-2-shows-a-look-back: Figure 3 in §5.2 shows a look-back after approximately frame 800. Table 1 measures overall long-video SSIM, LPIPS, style and reprojection, without a separate revisit success rate.
report.6-explicitly-focuses-on-static-en: §6 explicitly focuses on static environments without explicitly modeling dynamic scenes. Robot demonstrations exported to Isaac Sim do not establish an independent physics clock in the generation model itself.
report.a-three-js-engine-outputs-semanti: A Three.js engine outputs semantic frames. Streaming training and two-step distillation adapt MiniMax-H3, with fixed opening frames and recent history supporting continuation.

report.code-preserves-the-map-no-dedicat: · Code preserves the map; no dedicated long-term appearance revisit results

report.evidence-blog-2-1-2-3-3-1-limitat: Evidence: blog §2.1/2.3, §3.1, Limitations; no dedicated independent-clock evaluation, so this is not paper-validated evidence.
report.2-1-explicitly-states-that-return: §2.1 explicitly states that returning to the original position uses the same map and that physics and rules advance with fixed steps. This is an official technical blog claim.

report.published-repository-measurements: Published repository measurements use four held-out CARLA videos, each with 24 chunks, approximately 17 s and one random seed. Metrics are pixel MSE and runtime per chunk.
